title: Ops reliability sync playbook — 15-week tactical plan
content:
Purpose and context:

This is a working playbook for the next 15 weeks to synchronize SRE, platform, serving-runtime, product-hosted-api, and customer-success on SLO adoption, error-budget experiments, and runbook readiness. Goal is to move a set of 6 pilot services from ad-hoc SLOs -> repeatable SLO lifecycle (design -> monitor -> runbooks -> operational drills) with minimal product disruption.

High-level objectives (outcomes, not output):
- Pilot services have documented SLOs (latency & availability) and owner-approved error budgets.
- Dashboards and signal pipelines in place (Prometheus/Tempo/Vector -> Redwood console) for each pilot.
- Runbooks, canary thresholds, and rollback playbooks tested via table-top and 2 live canaries.
- A single cross-team playbook for oncall handoff, incident to SLO feedback, and weekly error-budget review.
- Identify 3 systemic platform changes (batching config, KV cache policy, routing fallback) to reduce tail latency risk.

Scope (what's in / out):
- In scope: 6 pilot services (listed below), latency p95/p99 and availability SLOs, dashboards, runbooks, canary plan, tabletop run.
- Out of scope: company-wide SLO rollout, billing/chargeback changes, private-deploy customers at this stage.

Pilot services (initial):
- hosted-api-route-a (product-team: hosted-api) — high-traffic text/generation route
- streaming-chat-proxy (product-team: console) — streaming path with long-lived connections
- embed-indexer (platform) — background batch + nearline embeddings
- model-serve-gateway (serving-runtime) — multi-model routing layer
- dedicated-pool-ingest (dedicated) — reserved GPU ingress pipeline
- telemetry-aggregator (infra) — processing of observability metrics

Stakeholders and roles (RACI-light):
- SRE lead (owner): Priya Menon — shepherd playbook, runbooks, tabletop schedule
- Product leads: Alex Chen (hosted-api), Samira Gomez (console) — approve SLO targets, manage product rollouts/canaries
- Platform/Infra: Derek Liu (platform-engineering) — implement dashboard signals, ensure routing fallbacks available
- Serving Runtime: Jordan Patel — quantify model-variant degradation impact, provide fallback variants
- CS / Customer Success: Maya Ortiz (advisory) — advise on customer SLAs and external comms

Milestones and 15-week sprint map (week numbers relative to start) — high level:
- Weeks 1–2: discovery, baseline signals, draft SLOs, stakeholder signoff
- Weeks 3–5: dashboard + alert plumbing; initial runbook templates; define canary criteria
- Weeks 6–8: implement light-weight canaries for 2 services; run tabletop for all 6; iterate SLO thresholds
- Weeks 9–11: error-budget policy experiments (throttle/re-route), implement telemetry improvements, triage results
- Weeks 12–13: follow-up canary (higher load), runbook dry-run with oncall swap; finalize documentation
- Weeks 14–15: retrospective, decision on scale-up for next cohort, capture playbook final edits

Sprint-by-sprint tactical tasks (sample):
Week 1:
- Kickoff: 60m cross-team sync (agenda: objectives, pilots, risks, owners). Owner: Priya
- Inventory: collect existing SLIs (latency histograms, availability windows) for each pilot. Owner: service owners
- Quick gap analysis: what signals are missing to compute p95/p99? Owner: Derek + Jordan

Week 2:
- Draft SLOs (template attached below) and circulate for 48h review. Owner: Product leads
- Create dashboard skeletons in shared Grafana/Console. Owner: Infra
- Add links to existing runbooks (if any) into a single index doc. Owner: Priya

Weeks 3–5 (monitoring + runbooks):
- Finalize SLIs and add alerts for SLO degradation (soft alert @50% of error budget, urgent at 80%).
- Build aggregated error-budget dashboard across pilots. Owner: Derek
- Runbook template: incident trigger -> triage checklist -> escalation steps -> customer comms draft. Owner: Priya + Jordan

Weeks 6–8 (canaries + tabletop):
- Canary plan 1 (low-risk): route 1% traffic to variant with stricter batching and observe p99 impact 48h. Owner: Product + Serving Runtime
- Tabletop (all teams): simulate p99 spike + partial regional outage; timeboxed 90 minutes. Owner: Priya
- Update runbooks after tabletop: record gaps, add decision trees.

Weeks 9–11 (experiments + telemetry fixes):
- Error-budget experiment: test automatic fallback to smaller model variant when p99 > threshold for > 10m. Rollback policy and safety gates required.
- Telemetry: add KV cache hit-rate SLI and compute correlation with tail-latency. Owner: Jordan

Weeks 12–15 (validation + handoff):
- High-load canary (10% traffic) for 24–48h on hosted-api-route-a. Stop conditions pre-defined.
- Oncall dry-run: SRE rotation swap with playbook-driven triage.
- Finalize playbook and publish to Confluence; prepare 1-pager for execs. Owner: Priya

Acceptance criteria (for promoting a pilot to “SLO-stable”):
- Documented SLO + agreed error budget policy (owner-approved).
- Dashboards show correct SLI values for ≥14 days (rolling window) and no missing telemetry gaps.
- Runbook exists and has been exercised in a tabletop or dry-run.
- Canary behavior is understood and rollback path proven in at least 1 low-risk canary.

Runbook template (short):
- Trigger: what signal(s) => e.g., p99 > 750ms for 5m or availability drop >1% in 5m
- Immediate triage: check ingress queue length; check GPU saturation; check routing errors; check KV cache hit-rate
- Quick fixes: route traffic to region B, increase dedicated pool concurrency, toggle batching param to conservative
- Escalation: Product lead -> Platform -> SRE oncall -> Engineering manager
- Communication: customer-facing status draft + internal incident channel template

Communication cadence and artifacts:
- Weekly error-budget sync (30m): owners only — quick status + action items. Friday 10:00 PT. Owner: Priya
- Biweekly cross-team review (60m): deeper analysis, experiment results, decisions. Owner: Alex
- Slack channels: #ops-slo-sync (alerts + summaries), #slo-breaches (auto-posts when urgent)
- Templates: status update, customer comms draft, runbook change PR template

SLO targets (starting proposals — to be tuned):
- Hosted-api-route-a: latency p95 < 250ms, p99 < 750ms; availability 99.95%
- Streaming-chat-proxy: availability 99.9% (streaming-specific jitter SLI TBC)
- Embed-indexer: job success rate 99.5% (nearline SLA), processing latency p95 < 5m
- Model-serve-gateway: p99 < 1s for routing + model-switching; availability 99.9%
- Dedicated-pool-ingest: pipeline success 99.6% (respecting capacity bursts)
- Telemetry-aggregator: metric ingestion 99.9% (30s window)

Risk register (top items):
- Missing telemetry for p99 (mitigation: short-term synthetic tests + add histogram buckets). Owner: Derek
- Canary harm: canaries inadvertently impact customer traffic (mitigation: strict stop conditions, rollback playbook, initial 1% cap). Owner: Product leads
- Cross-team bandwidth: teams deprioritize (mitigation: exec sponsor + weekly progress highlights). Owner: Priya
- Model variant quality trade-offs: fallback variants degrade user experience (mitigation: quality gates and A/B analysis). Owner: Jordan

Success metrics and KPIs for program (how we measure program-level success):
- Number of pilots promoted to SLO-stable within 15 weeks (target: 4/6)
- Reduction in p99 across pilots after experiments (target: 15% median reduction)
- Time to detect SLO breach (baseline -> target < 2 minutes)
- % of incidents with SLO-root-cause identified within 72h (target: 90%)

Open questions / decisions to resolve in Week 1:
- How strictly do product partners want to treat availability vs latency tradeoffs during canaries? (Product owners to confirm)
- Do we centralize error-budget policies (automatic throttles) or keep policy per-service? (Ops/Platform decision)
- Is there a requirement to notify customers at 50% error-budget usage? (CS advise needed)

Checklist before any canary: (must be green)
- [ ] Rollback steps documented and tested in staging
- [ ] Stop conditions defined and automated where possible
- [ ] Monitoring in place for p95/p99/availability + infra signals (GPU temp, queue depth)
- [ ] Pager rules configured and oncall briefed

Quick templates (copyable) — SLO draft header:
SLO name: <service> - latency / availability
Owner: <name>
Objective: p95 < X ms, p99 < Y ms, availability >= Z%
Error budget: 1 - availability (ex: 0.05% per 30d)
Escalation policy: auto-notify @50% budget, require human intervention @80%

Notes to self: keep this doc alive, track decisions in the decision-log table in Confluence, do not lock down SLO numbers until after 2 weeks of baseline data. Use tabletop findings to build a short list of platform fixes that will buy the most headroom (likely KV cache tweaks and routing fallbacks).

Links and references (working):
- Incident taxonomy (confluence) — https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Incident+Taxonomy
- Existing runbook index — (attach link after week1 inventory)
- Experiment PR for routing fallback — https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/678

Next immediate actions (owner in parens):
- Schedule kickoff (Priya) — done? pending calendar invite
- Each pilot owner: paste current SLIs into the shared sheet and mark gaps (service owners)
- Infra: spin up dashboard skeletons and share links before end of week (Derek)

-- end --
